newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal denies its arms smuggled to Rwandans.
newsitem.headline: Portugal denies its arms smuggled to Rwandans.

text.p: Portugal on Monday denied a report that Portuguese rifles could have been sent on a flight from Madrid to eastern Zaire in May 1994 said to have been carrying arms bound for exiled Rwandan Hutus.

Spanish newspaper El Pais on Sunday quoted a U.N. report as saying second hand Portuguese G-3 rifles might have been included in the 39 tonnes of arms sent on board a Nigerian-registered plane in violation of a U.N. arms embargo.

A Portuguese spokeswoman said the government had sent a letter to the U.N.'s International Commission of Inquiry for Rwanda that said the serial numbers on the rifles that were found did not correspond to those manufactured in Portugal.

The letter, dated September 30, responded to a question from the Commission, which El Pais said had listed the serial numbers of the G-3 rifles found in Iwawa, Rwanda in November 1995 after a battle between Hutu militias and Tutsi troops.

"Our letter said that the only factory that produces G-3 rifles in Portugal uses an exclusive serial number with six digits. These were not the serial numbers that were listed," the Foreign Ministry spokeswoman told Reuters.

"This verifies that the G-3 rifles concerned were not produced in Portugal. The weapons do not form part of the Portuguese armed forces' inventories. That is, they were not stolen from our armed forces," she added.
In Madrid, a Foreign Ministry spokeswoman said on Sunday that Spain had informed the United Nations that the plane under investigation for shipping arms to Rwanda carried only food.
The U.N. commission is trying to uncover the activities of former Rwandan army colonel Theoneste Bagosera, who ordered weapons for exiled Hutus in complicity with Zairean officials, El Pais reported.

Bagosera has been accused of playing a central role in the 1994 genocide of one million Rwandan Tutsis and of trying to re-arm the exiled resistance to the Tutsi-led force that became the present Rwandan government.
He is believed to have boarded the plane in question in Malta. The shipment was made a month after the massacres of minority Rwandan Tutsis had begun.
Bagosera is now in jail in Cameroon after Belgium requested his detention and extradition on charges that he killed 10 Belgian U.N. peacekeepers based in Rwanda in April 1994.
